params.body:
## What

`rules/trend.json#holds` gets two numbers: a trend holds only when at least 3 of its signals support it outright (`minFullSupports`), from at least 2 distinct sources (`minFullSupportSources`). The 0.10.0 bar (5 supporting, partly counted half, from 3 sources) stays.

- `tools/rules.mjs`: `trendHolds` applies both; its answer keeps the same shape (`holds`, `supporting`, `sources`, `state`).
- `tools/check.mjs`: refuses a holds rule without the two numbers, or one asking more outright supports than supporting signals.
- `conformance/rules.json`: three new cases (one support and ten partly: lead; three supports from one source: lead; three supports from two sources plus partly: holds).
- VERSION 0.11.0, CHANGELOG, exports regenerated.

## Why

The first trends judged under 0.10.0 (14 October 2026) included one with 84 signals: 1 supports, 10 partly, 73 unrelated. Ten halves and one whole made 6 supporting from 8 sources, so it held, and the Studio would have offered it to writers as a finding. That is the thin-but-presented-as-strong case 0.10.0 was written to stop. Partial matches now add up but cannot carry a trend alone.

A rule's number changed, so this is a minor version (VERSIONING.md).

## Checks

- `npm run check`: standard ok
- `npm test`: 75 of 75 pass
- `npm run compat`: compatible with v0.1.0 through v0.10.0

After merge: tag v0.11.0 on the merge commit; the pipeline then moves its pin from v0.10.0 to v0.11.0 in its own PR.
params.title: 0.11.0 (proposed): a trend holds on outright support, not on partial matches
